trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and it asks for everything: the other 54 trophies, which means the full story, the 100% completion checklist and every side feat in Leonida. There is no shortcut and no online requirement — the whole list is single-player. Work the roadmap in order: story first, protecting the one possibly-missable meditation in Chapter 1, then the 100% checklist, then cleanup. Launch guides put the full road at roughly 200 hours at about 4/10 difficulty, so treat it as a marathon you chip at with this tracker. When the 54th trophy lands, this one follows on its own.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The first trophy of the game: finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission. It is on the story's critical path and cannot be missed — play through the introduction and it pops as the mission closes. Because GTA VI has no mission replay, nothing later can block it either. Start your save discipline here: make a first manual save right after this mission, and keep one at the start of every chapter. That habit is what protects the one fragile trophy window that opens later in Chapter 1, around Lucia's meditation at Jason's house.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 1. Chapter trophies can pop at the start of the next chapter rather than on the last cutscene, so do not worry if this one lands a few minutes late. Chapter 1 holds the game's one fragile moment: after the mission Down to Earth, Lucia talks about meditating at Jason's house in the morning and walks out to the balcony. Follow her and accept before the chapter ends — see Positive Mental Attitude — and keep a Chapter 1 manual save until that trophy is safe. Everything else in the chapter can be revisited in free roam.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. The asterisks are PlayStation's own — the name is published censored, so it is reproduced here exactly as published, not cleaned up. Chapter 2 is where the game opens out: character switching unlocks after Breakfast Run, and with it the partner trophies, while the Scooter Bros and real-estate apps that later trophies need come online during this stretch. Keep a manual save at the chapter boundary, and start scanning traffic with the WAiNK app as you drive — the vehicle discoveries you bank now pay off in the Stage 2 checklist.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3. This chapter hands you the robbery toolkit: Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs gives you the Snap Gun and opens jewelry stores for Sneakthief, and Yago's street-racing strand brings Race Against Yago — a time-sensitive race that counts toward Strangers & Freaks, so run it the moment it appears rather than parking it. Nothing about the chapter trophy itself can be missed; it follows the story. Keep the usual discipline anyway: a fresh manual save at the chapter start, because no story mission in this game can be replayed.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4. Near the end of this chapter the optional mission That's Where The Money Is opens bank-vault robberies — the engine behind Maximum Withdrawal, and a reliable way to earn Hot Together on the escape with your partner. If you would rather finish the story first, the vaults stay available afterwards; nothing in Chapter 4 is missable. Two standing rules apply here as everywhere: keep a manual save from the chapter start, and never use cheats on your trophy save — launch guides report they switch off trophies and saving.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission — the gold that closes the campaign. Before you start it, park a manual save in its own slot and never overwrite it: with no mission replay and no New Game Plus, that save is your only way back to a pre-ending world state. The trophy itself is unmissable once you commit to the ending. After the credits, the 100% checklist appears under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion, and every side strand, robbery and free-roam trophy stays open — the story ending is the start of Stage 2, not the end of the road.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Its real reward is mechanical: finishing it unlocks switching between Jason and Lucia, and from then on you can call the other lead in as your partner — the gate behind Hot Together, Retail Therapy and meditating at a spot with both characters for double counter credit. The mission itself is unmissable story progress. If any partner trophy is in your plan, push the story at least this far early, even if you mostly intend to free-roam; a whole wing of the list waits behind this one mission.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, a Chapter 3 story mission. It is on the critical path and cannot be missed — finish the heist and the trophy follows, with no medal or performance requirement attached. Treat it as rehearsal for the free-roam robbery trophies: the jewelry, shop and vault jobs you unlock around this part of the game all reuse the same rhythm of grab, run and lose the heat. On the roadmap it pops naturally during Stage 1, so there is no detour to plan — just do not let your chapter saves lapse around it.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. This is an unmissable mid-story beat: the trophy asks only that the mission be finished, and no launch source reports a fail state or a choice that can lock it away. trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — the long gold, and the real spine of the platinum. The checklist only appears after the story, under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion, but work you do earlier still counts toward it. As the launch guides report the checklist, its headline demands are fractions rather than totals: 200 of 277 vehicles discovered, 100 of 255 animals studied, 70 of 80 Challenges, 300 stunts (past the 250 the stunt trophy itself needs), 15 of 18 meditations, all eight bank vaults and one robbed operation per gang on the way to all 39. Plan Stage 2 around this checklist and let the individual trophies fall out of the grind.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. 'Stunts' is a family, not one trick: stunt jumps, under-the-bridge flights, knife flights and base jumps all feed the same counter, so vary your routes and grab them as you cross the map rather than grinding one ramp. Two numbers matter: 250 earns this trophy, but the 100% checklist wants 300, so do not stop at the trophy — the counter in this guide runs to 250 for the trophy, and A Long Road will ask for 50 more. Most stunts are one-attempt landmarks; a failed jump can simply be re-driven.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once — the game has nine activity types, and a single attempt at each is all this trophy asks. You do not need to win, medal or finish first; you need to have genuinely tried each type once. Activity types unlock as the map and story open up (fishing, racing, the shooting range, arcade games and more), so sweep this up as you travel rather than hunting it in one session. If one type seems missing late in the game, it is usually a strand or app you have not opened yet — the story unlocks several of them.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — 42 golds in all, spread across the game's two shooting ranges. Each challenge scores you on its own terms, so learn one challenge's target pattern at a time and replay it until the gold lands; medals are permanent once earned, and the counter in this guide pane lets you tick off each gold as it comes. This is one of the few trophies that tests execution rather than patience, so if a challenge resists, come back with better weapons and a cooler head rather than forcing it.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — 14 locations across Leonida, and one win at each is enough. The locations are spread the length of the state, so treat this as a travelling trophy: clear a location's race when your route passes it rather than saving all fourteen for one grind. A lost race costs nothing but the retry, and the drone handling you learn at the early locations makes the later ones much easier. Tick each location off in the counter here so the last two or three stragglers are easy to identify at cleanup.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word that matters is 'different': repeating one easy race twenty times earns nothing, so keep a spread — street races and the other race types as they unlock across the map. Yago's time-sensitive Chapter 3 race is one of the twenty if you catch it, and it also feeds a Strangers & Freaks strand, which makes it the best-value race on the list. Races you lose can be retried freely. Use the counter here to track distinct wins, because the game will happily let you re-win a favourite and feel more progress than you have made.

trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the game's activity types, and Cal's challenge is offered early — launch checklists already list 'beat Cal at fishing' among the things you can do in Chapter 1. trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida — and read the warning first, because this is the list's one possibly-missable trophy. The PlayStation counter runs to 18. The danger: in Chapter 1, after Down to Earth, Lucia meditates on the balcony at Jason's house one morning — follow her from the kitchen and accept, because that session is gone after Chapter 1. It raises the counter but is not marked like the other spots, and whether the trophy strictly needs it is unconfirmed; do it anyway and keep a Chapter 1 save. One honest conflict: the in-game 100% checklist asks for 15 meditations while the PSN counter runs to 18 — the trophy follows the counter.

trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret Vogel's hunting questline is Jason-only and works through target decks: he sends you after specific animals, and this trophy is the strand's signature kill — a unique animal he asks for by name. When the hunt comes, take the clean shot: a head or heart shot keeps the carcass pristine, which is what a trophy hunt is judged on. The strand sits in Stage 3 cleanup in this roadmap because it is self-contained — pick it up when you want a change of pace from the robbery set, and study animals with binoculars on the way for the 100% checklist.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three Collectible Card sets. Cards are one of Leonida's collectible families: individual cards are gathered out in the world and a set completes when you hold every card in it, so progress is lumpy — long quiet stretches, then a set closes. Work them into your Stage 2 travel rather than hunting them in isolation, and tick each finished set off in the counter here. One honesty note: at launch, none of the sources this guide cites has published a verified full card map, so any exact card location you read elsewhere should be treated as unconfirmed until the trackers catch up — this guide will not invent locations to look complete.

trophies.guide: Lose a four-star Wanted Level with your partner beside you and fully escape the heat. trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Rob three shops back-to-back with your partner, without your Wanted Level ever dropping in between. trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies inside a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-motion aim: press L3 and R3 together while aiming. Do not improvise the crowd — set the shot up where enemies gather in the open, such as the guards at a gang's illegal operation, and bring an assault rifle so the five kills fit inside one Focus window. Adrenaline extends Focus, so a full meter is your friend. If the fifth takedown keeps slipping out of the window, soften the group up first and let Focus finish them; the counter here tracks your best single-window count.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA: steal a large passenger plane that is docked at a boarding bridge and take off in it. Climb in, back out toward the runway and get airborne, then keep flying: the trophy is delayed and pops roughly a kilometre away from the airport. Save before you try, because the police response at an international airport is fast and a busted attempt costs real time.

Save before you make the trip — a military base is not a forgiving place to improvise — then get in, drive and fire until the trophy pops. It is a one-off feat rather than a grind: a single good run at the base should do it, and the trip doubles as exploration progress toward The Goodtime State.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. The toolkit arrives in Chapter 3: the mission Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs gives you the Snap Gun and opens jewelry-store robberies. Go to a store's locked back door and use the Snap Gun on it — kicking the door in sets off the alarm and ends the attempt. In the back room, find the note carrying the safe code, open the safe and leave unseen. Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds in Vice City is a reported good target. If someone spots you, reload and rerun it clean rather than pushing on; an undetected job is the whole trophy.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape from each. Vaults unlock through That's Where The Money Is, an optional mission near the end of Chapter 4: tail an armored security van to a large bank and get into the vault while the guard has it open. Bring your partner — you cannot carry all the money bags alone. Every vault job starts your escape at four stars, so plan the getaway before you plan the grab, and remember the escape only counts once you are fully out of the heat. Five vaults earn the trophy; the 100% checklist wants all eight, so finish the set while you are warmed up.

The stragglers at cleanup are predictable — far islands, swamp interiors and the corners no mission visits — so when the counter stalls in the high forties, tour the map's edges rather than its roads. Exploration also feeds everything else: stunts, WAiNK locations and meditation spots all live out where this trophy sends you.

trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from bank and payday-loan jobs, and they are only worth anything once your contacts have laundered them — so the trophy measures a pipeline, not a single score: rob, collect marked bills, sell them on through your contacts, repeat. The $250,000 total is cumulative, which makes this a companion to Maximum Withdrawal and Pest Control rather than a separate campaign: every vault and loan job you work in Stage 2 and 3 feeds it. Use the money counter here to mirror your laundered total, not your cash on hand — unwashed bills do not count.
